hypotheses.claim: The recent in‑memory check‑then‑act implementation (without locking) introduced a race condition that allowed concurrent reservations to oversell SKU‑901, producing negative inventory.
hypotheses.supporting_reasoning: EV-CODE-002 and EV-CODE-003 show the new code reads stock, checks it, then writes back without any atomic guarantee. EV-MET-001 records a sudden surge to 50 concurrent checkout threads, providing the concurrency needed for interleaved executions. EV-MET-002 and EV-MET-003 document spikes in oversold units and reconciliation errors that coincide with the code change, linking the non‑atomic logic to the observed negative stock.
falsification_criteria: If a controlled single‑threaded test of the new code never produces a negative stock value, the hypothesis is falsified
If logs from a replicated environment show that all stock updates are serialized at the database level despite the in‑memory logic, the hypothesis is falsified
verification_plan: Review the implementation of get_stock, set_stock, and reservation handling to confirm absence of mutexes or DB transactions
Instrument the reservation path to record timestamps of read‑check‑write sequences under high concurrency
Replay the incident window with a load generator using the new code and verify whether negative stock occurs
Revert the code to the original atomic DB decrement (as in EV-CODE-001) and confirm that oversell disappears

hypotheses.claim: Transient Redis replica replication delays caused workers to read stale stock values, leading to reservations being approved based on outdated inventory and resulting in oversell.
hypotheses.supporting_reasoning: EV-LOG-003 notes a 12 ms replication ping delay, indicating that replica data may lag behind the primary. EV-MET-001 shows a spike to 50 concurrent checkout threads, increasing the chance that some workers read from a lagging replica during the surge, which could explain the mismatch between reported stock (10) and reservations (18).
falsification_criteria: If the inventory service is confirmed to read exclusively from the primary database during the incident window, the hypothesis is falsified
If replication lag measurements during the spike remain below the time needed for a reservation transaction, the hypothesis is falsified
verification_plan: Determine the data source used by get_stock (primary DB vs Redis replica) during reservation processing
Measure real‑time replication lag of the Redis replica during a simulated load matching EV-MET-001
Force the service to read only from the primary and repeat the high‑concurrency test to see if oversell persists
Introduce artificial replication delay and observe whether oversell frequency changes

hypotheses.claim: The removal of the atomic database decrement guard eliminated a built‑in safety check, allowing stock to be decremented below zero even in the absence of concurrency.
hypotheses.supporting_reasoning: EV-CODE-001 documents the prior safe atomic decrement operation that inherently prevented negative stock. EV-CODE-002 shows that this operation was replaced with an in‑memory check‑then‑act pattern lacking any database‑level guard, meaning a single reservation could potentially drive stock negative if the guard logic is flawed or bypassed.
falsification_criteria: If database constraints or triggers still prevent stock from dropping below zero despite the code change, the hypothesis is falsified
If a single‑threaded execution of the new code never produces a negative stock value, the hypothesis is falsified
verification_plan: Inspect the database schema for constraints that enforce non‑negative stock values
Execute a single‑threaded reservation for SKU‑901 using the new code and verify the resulting stock level
Re‑introduce the atomic decrement (as in EV-CODE-001) in a test environment and confirm that negative stock no longer occurs
Review unit and integration test coverage to ensure the guard logic is exercised
